tasks.description: Add the two live-check folders under task-formats/blend
Write the port conformance test for the probes the spine relies on
Create the machine generator with regions, ids, meta and tags
Add the readiness and cascade rows and the dependency tags
Add the outcome region driven by active.onDone
Add the history, cause, time and span actions
Replace the four machines and the fold code with the snapshot engine API
Update the engine tests into fact sequences with the classification list
Update the random fold test and add the AD-5 fold tests
Add the progress alphabet and the walk key
Write the graph proof with its negative control and reduction check
Update the runner to the phase-1 seam on the run snapshot
Update the status projection to read the snapshot through view
Add the delegate helper and the phase-1 task-ui check
Update the conformance harness for the phase-1 engine and pass H1–H16
Write the state audit with the AD-17 entries and the interim allowlist
Add task.nudged and the run path to the fact list
Implement the AD-13 status contract and the shared status fixture
Create the Recorder and the status writer
Create the TaskHarness service with leases and the session index
Add the HarnessHooks routing beside the hook maps
Create the stateless workers and the session-events actor
Create the task supervisor with the event-driven builder watch
Create the scenario supervisor with its judge round
Create the run supervisor with its parallel timer regions
Wire the command, the hooks and SessionPrompt onto the harness in one cut-over
Remove the polled runner, the hook maps and the polled builder watch
Validate the final phase-2 allowlist of the state audit
Update the conformance harness for the actors and pass H1–H16
Update the VERIFY.md schema so that ensures is required
Update the command to list every loader failure in the refusal
Add spec.checked and the run warning for a spec that stops validating
Add external regions and the subtree refusal
Add the six fault folders under task-formats/blend
Write the fault-folder test that runs the real /task command on each folder
Validate that both live-check folders still load once ensures is required
Update the graph proof to walk the fault-folder plans that load
Add scripted end-to-end runs of the two live-check folders
Update task-demo.sh to copy every example folder
Write the Validation section of the blend README
Create the taskView machine and the fromActor adapter
Update the store to decode AD-13 and classify only from tags
Wire the plugin, the watch and the Peek polls onto the view actor
Create the shared region and mount it in every expanded view
Update the Peek BUILDER heading with reasons, waits and durations
Update the Board and the Matrix to read tags, causes and durations
Update the Gantt and the HUD to draw spans and durations
Update the Ledger, Dock, Ticker and full-screen header
Update the shortcut bar and animate the In the Flow mark
Add the run header with the spec title from structured metadata
Add Ops.say and the closing summary written by the run supervisor
Add the run usage to the prompt footer, the sidebar and the task-ui
Validate the final state audit with task-ui in scope and update the task-ui README
Validate the quality gate on the final branch

scenarios.description: The blend format README answers questions 1, 3 and 4 in a Validation section
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: DOC1 The blend format README answers questions 1, 3 and 4 in a Validation section
    Given the blend format README
    When a reader opens its Validation section
    Then it says what runs before any work starts and how a refusal appears
    And it lists every rule R1 to R13 with the place that enforces it
    And it says how the run machine holds the order and which graph faults are refused
    And it names the six fault folders and the two live-check folders

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Phase 1 — one run machine (AC 2-6)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: One machine is generated for each plan with a parallel region for every unit
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM1 One machine is generated for each plan with a parallel region for every unit
    Given the release-notes plan
    When the engine generates the run machine for it
    Then its root is parallel with the regions active and outcome
    And active holds one region for each task in plan order, then each scenario, then each outside precondition
    And each task region is parallel with one evidence sub-region for each obligation and a work sub-region
    And every unit state has an explicit id, a meta record of unit, kind and state, and only closed-vocabulary tags

  @phase1 @negative

scenarios.description: The generator refuses a machine it cannot fold safely
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM2 The generator refuses a machine it cannot fold safely
    Given a plan whose task ids give two equal explicit state ids
    When the engine generates the run machine
    Then the generation dies naming the repeated id
    And every generated machine caps eventless iterations at 1000
    And no generated machine for any plan has a delayed transition, an invoked actor, a spawned actor or a custom action

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: The per-unit machines and the fold code that joined them are gone
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM3 The per-unit machines and the fold code that joined them are gone
    Given the engine module after the change
    When its exports and definitions are inspected
    Then no obligation, task, scenario or run machine exists beside the generated machine
    And no stepTask, stepRun, cancel, staleAlone or follows code exists
    And XStateEngine keeps its name and its initial and apply members over an opaque snapshot

  @phase1 @audit

scenarios.description: Every old engine test is ported, re-baselined or retired with its reason (owner ruling 2)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM4 Every old engine test is ported, re-baselined or retired with its reason (owner ruling 2)
    Given the engine test file after the rewrite
    When its header list is read
    Then every test of the old file appears once as ported, re-baselined or retired
    And each re-baselined test names the decision or owner ruling that changed it
    And each retired test names the guard that replaces it
    And every listed test runs as a fact sequence through initial, apply and the selectors

  @phase1 @integrity

scenarios.description: A fold, a live actor and a resumed actor reach the same snapshot
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM5 A fold, a live actor and a resumed actor reach the same snapshot
    Given 40 seeded sequences of 100 random facts over the release-notes plan, including facts after the run ended
    When each sequence is folded with apply and also sent to a live actor of the same machine
    And a prefix is folded, restored into an actor, and sent the rest of the sequence
    Then the three snapshots are equal for every sequence
    And the log grows exactly when the state or another context field changes

  @phase1 @integrity

scenarios.description: Apply is pure and guards its input
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM6 Apply is pure and guards its input
    Given a snapshot of a running release-notes run
    When a fact that matches no row is applied
    Then the identical snapshot is returned and the input is not mutated
    And a fact applied to a snapshot whose run has ended returns that snapshot unchanged
    And a snapshot made by another machine makes apply die

  @phase1 @core @critical

scenarios.description: The observed stuck run blocks its dependants in the same fold step
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM7 The observed stuck run blocks its dependants in the same fold step
    Given the release-notes plan and the observed facts up to the second failing proof of T1.4
    When the third failing proof of T1.4 is applied
    Then T1.4 is budget exhausted
    And T1.5 and T1 are blocked in the snapshot that apply returns
    And each of T1.5 and T1 has a history entry whose reason is "blocked by T1.4: budget exhausted"
    And T1.5 and T1 carry the blocked cause T1.4 in state budget_exhausted

  @phase1 @compat

scenarios.description: An old slice that ended folds with its stop's state, and /task starts a new slice
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM8a An old slice that ended folds with its stop's state, and /task starts a new slice
    Given a stored slice written by the old engine, with run.started without a path and run.ended in state done
    When the slice is folded through the new machine and /task runs on the whole spec
    Then every stored fact decodes and folds, and the stored run.ended folds as a stop with its own state
    And /task records run.started for a new slice, because the old slice ended

  @phase1 @compat

scenarios.description: An old slice with no end and no path resumes on /task of the whole spec
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM8b An old slice with no end and no path resumes on /task of the whole spec
    Given a stored slice written by the old engine, with run.started without a path, no run.ended, and a fold that is not done
    When /task runs on the whole spec, also when the path is written ./<spec>/
    Then the slice counts as a whole-spec slice and the run resumes
    And the resume records only run.resumed with the path, a fact type that already exists

  @phase1 @compat

scenarios.description: The observed stuck slice folds to its end and is never resumed
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM8c The observed stuck slice folds to its end and is never resumed
    Given the observed facts stored with no run.ended
    When the slice is folded through the new machine
    Then the fold is done with the outcome budget exhausted, and T1.5 and T1 are blocked
    And /task on the same spec starts a new slice and never resumes a done fold

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: The cascade is transitive and names the first dead dependency
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM9 The cascade is transitive and names the first dead dependency
    Given a plan where T3 is after T2, T2 is after T1, and scenario S1 needs T3
    When T1 fails
    Then T2 is blocked by T1 and T3 is blocked by T2 in the same fold step
    And S1 is blocked by T3
    And a task with two dead dependencies names the first one in dependency order

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: Independent work runs to its end before the run settles
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM10 Independent work runs to its end before the run settles
    Given a plan with two independent leaves T1.1 and T1.2, both building
    When T1.1 is budget exhausted
    Then the run keeps running while T1.2 builds, proves and is verified
    And the run settles only when T1.2 reaches a final state
    And the run outcome is then budget exhausted

  @phase1 @core @negative

scenarios.description: The outcome is the state of the task that died first, and the reason lists every dead and blocked task
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM11 The outcome is the state of the task that died first, and the reason lists every dead and blocked task
    Given a run where T1.1 needs a human first, T1.2 fails later, and T1.3 is blocked by T1.1
    When every region is final
    Then the run outcome is needs human
    And the run reason has one line for T1.1, one line for T1.2, then one line "T1.3 blocked by T1.1"

  @phase1 @core @negative

scenarios.description: A rejected runnable scenario fails a run whose tasks are all trusted (owner ruling 1)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM12 A rejected runnable scenario fails a run whose tasks are all trusted (owner ruling 1)
    Given a run where every task is trusted
    When a runnable scenario is rejected by its verifier
    Then the run outcome is failed
    And the run reason has the line "acceptance not proved: <scenario id> rejected"

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: A scenario that waits only on an outside precondition is parked and does not fail the run (owner ruling 1)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM13 A scenario that waits only on an outside precondition is parked and does not fail the run (owner ruling 1)
    Given the release-notes plan with T9 trusted and T8 untrusted
    When every task is trusted and every runnable scenario is trusted
    Then S13 is parked and shows as waiting
    And the run outcome is done with the reason line "not run: S13 waits on T8"
    And when T8 is trusted before the run settles, S13 moves from parked to ready

  @phase1 @core @edge

scenarios.description: A cancel moves every unfinished unit to cancelled and keeps the finished ones (default 4)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM14 A cancel moves every unfinished unit to cancelled and keeps the finished ones (default 4)
    Given a run with a trusted task, a building task, a ready task and a waiting task
    When the run is cancelled with a reason
    Then the building, ready and waiting tasks are cancelled with that reason
    And the trusted task stays trusted, and every obligation keeps its state and ends with its task
    And the run outcome is cancelled with that reason, because no task died before the stop
    And a run wall-clock stop gives the run.ended state as the outcome in the same way

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: A task becomes ready only when every after task and every child is trusted
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM15 A task becomes ready only when every after task and every child is trusted
    Given the release-notes plan
    When T1.1 is trusted and T1.2 is not
    Then T1.3 is ready and T1.4 is waiting
    And the parent T1 is waiting until every child is trusted
    And when a trusted dependency goes stale, a ready dependant returns to waiting

  @phase1 @core @concurrency

scenarios.description: Two siblings with no order between them become ready in the same step
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM16 Two siblings with no order between them become ready in the same step
    Given a plan with leaves T1.1, T1.2 after T1.1, and T1.3 after T1.1
    When the fact that makes T1.1 trusted is applied
    Then T1.2 and T1.3 are both ready in the snapshot that apply returns

  @phase1 @core @edge

scenarios.description: A task waiting on an untrusted outside precondition stays waiting and moves on its trust
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM17 A task waiting on an untrusted outside precondition stays waiting and moves on its trust
    Given the release-notes plan with T1.1 to T1.4 trusted, every scenario whose needs are trusted also trusted, and T9 untrusted
    When the snapshot is read
    Then T1.5 is waiting, its waitingOn names T9, and the run is waiting, not ended
    And when outside.trusted for T9 is applied, T1.5 becomes ready
    And a second trust of T9 changes nothing

  @phase1 @core

scenarios.description: The phase-1 runner reads readiness and completion from the machine
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM18 The phase-1 runner reads readiness and completion from the machine
    Given the runner after phase 1
    When a run proceeds
    Then the runner starts a task only when the snapshot tags it ready
    And the runner keeps no readiness check, no outside trust set and no done decision of its own
    And the runner never records run.ended in state done
    And the runner stops when the snapshot status is done

  @phase1 @proof @ASSUMPTION:A1.a

scenarios.description: The graph walk finds no stuck state in the release-notes plan (owner ruling 4)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM19 The graph walk finds no stuck state in the release-notes plan (owner ruling 4)
    Given the release-notes plan and the engine's progress alphabet
    When every state reachable with the canonical interleaving is walked within 60 seconds
    Then no state that is not done lacks an event that changes its key
    And every visited snapshot has status active or done

  @phase1 @proof @ASSUMPTION:A1.a

scenarios.description: The graph walk finds no stuck state in the two live-check plans
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM20 The graph walk finds no stuck state in the two live-check plans
    Given the loaded plans of the two live-check folders, and from phase 3 the whole outside-run plan and its T1.2 subtree
    When each plan is walked within 60 seconds
    Then each walk finds no stuck state

  @phase1 @proof @ASSUMPTION:A1.a

scenarios.description: The graph walk finds the observed stuck state when the cascade rows are removed
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM21 The graph walk finds the observed stuck state when the cascade rows are removed
    Given a copy of the release-notes machine config without the blocked rows
    When the copy is walked
    Then the walk reports a stuck state with T1.1 to T1.3 trusted, T1.4 budget exhausted, and T1.5 and T1 waiting

  @phase1 @proof @ASSUMPTION:A1.a

scenarios.description: The walk's reduction and key are sound (owner ruling 4)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM22 The walk's reduction and key are sound (owner ruling 4)
    Given a small plan
    When the canonical walk and the full walk run with and without the blocked rows
    Then both walks find the same set of stuck states
    And the stale walk of the loaded example-cascade plan finds no stuck state
    And every context path that a guard reads is part of the walk key

  @phase1 @compat

scenarios.description: The port behaves as the spine relies on
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM23 The port behaves as the spine relies on
    Given the pinned xstate port
    When the 2026-10-14 probes run
    Then a state id is split on dots, a final state inside a parallel region still takes events, and an onDone target re-enters the region
    And a pure transition on a done snapshot still runs a microstep, and raised and done events carry no time
    And snapshot tags are an array, an eventless loop past the iteration cap fails, and the walk limit counts edges

  @phase1 @compat

scenarios.description: During phase 1 the status file shows a blocked task with its cause
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM24 During phase 1 the status file shows a blocked task with its cause
    Given a phase-1 run that folds the observed facts
    When the status file is written
    Then T1.5 and T1 have the state blocked and the reason "blocked by T1.4: budget exhausted"
    And the status file keeps every field it had before the change


  @phase1 @integrity

scenarios.description: Start times, end times and spans come only from machine actions
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM25 Start times, end times and spans come only from machine actions
    Given the loaded example-cascade plan and facts with fixed times
    When T1.1 builds and fails its proof, and T1.3 builds and is trusted
    Then T1.1 has its start time at task.started, its end time at the failing proof, and the spans waiting, building, proving and a zero-length budget_exhausted
    And the blocked T1.2 has an end time and no start time
    And a stale obligation on the trusted T1.3 clears its end time and starts its clock again

  @phase1 @compat

scenarios.description: The unchanged task-ui shows a phase-1 blocked task with its cause
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM26 The unchanged task-ui shows a phase-1 blocked task with its cause
    Given the phase-1 status of the observed facts
    When the task-ui of the checkpoint renders it on the Board
    Then T1.5 and T1 sit in STOPPED with the label blocked
    And each card shows "blocked by T1.4: budget exhausted"

  @phase1 @core @edge

scenarios.description: A task that died before a stop gives the end state, and the stop cancels unfinished units (AC 4, default 4)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM27 A task that died before a stop gives the end state, and the stop cancels unfinished units (AC 4, default 4)
    Given T1.1 budget exhausted, T1.4 blocked by T1.1, an independent T1.2 building, and S1 waiting
    When run.cancelled is applied with the reason "user stop"
    Then the run outcome is budget exhausted, the state of the task that died first
    And the run reason holds the line for T1.1, then the line "T1.4 blocked by T1.1", then the line "user stop"
    And T1.2 and S1 are cancelled, and T1.1 stays budget exhausted

  @phase1 @negative

scenarios.description: A machine error is a defect, never a frozen run
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM28 A machine error is a defect, never a frozen run
    Given a generated machine whose guard names a state id that does not exist, reachable only after task.started
    When task.started is applied
    Then apply dies with a defect that names the error
    And apply never returns a snapshot whose status is error
    And the generator's config scan refuses any stateIn id that names no state

  @phase1 @proof

scenarios.description: A gap in the generated rows fails the structural totality check before any run (owner ruling 4)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: RM29 A gap in the generated rows fails the structural totality check before any run (owner ruling 4)
    Given a copy of the release-notes machine config with the row that blocks T1.5 on T1.4 budget exhausted removed
    When the generator's totality check scans the copy
    Then it fails with an error that names T1.5, its waiting state and the uncovered outcome T1.4 budget exhausted
    And the scan of every real plan passes: each non-final unit state has a row for every final outcome of what it waits on
    And no non-final state lacks a way out except a wait on an untrusted outside or external region, and the outcome can settle once every region is final
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Phase 2 — live supervision as actors (AC 8-11)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: The runner holds no hand-written lifecycle state
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV1 The runner holds no hand-written lifecycle state
    Given the harness source after phase 2
    When it is inspected
    Then it holds no polled loop, tick counter, stale cadence counter, failure map, failure limit, stopping flag, children list, worker FiberMap, judged-state list or process-wide run registry
    And a live run is found through the actor system by its run id

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: The run supervisor starts work from the machine's tags and records every outcome as a fact
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV2 The run supervisor starts work from the machine's tags and records every outcome as a fact
    Given a run with a ready leaf and a verifying scenario
    When the run supervisor reads the run actor
    Then it spawns one task supervisor for the leaf and one scenario supervisor for the scenario
    And each supervisor records the outcome of its phase as a fact through the Recorder
    And a supervisor stops when its unit leaves the ready, active and verifying tags
    And the run machine itself invokes nothing

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: A run resumes only by the same path (owner ruling 3)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV3 A run resumes only by the same path (owner ruling 3)
    Given a stored slice that has not ended, started by /task with a path
    When /task runs again with the same path
    Then the slice is folded, run.resumed is recorded with that path, and the supervisor starts what the folded state asks for
    And /task with a different path, or after the slice ended, starts a new slice

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: Cancelling the job records the cancel even while a stale check runs
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV4 Cancelling the job records the cancel even while a stale check runs
    Given a live run whose run supervisor is checking the spec under the checkout lock
    When the background job is cancelled
    Then run.cancelled is in the store and in the status file
    And the run scope closes only after the run supervisor is final or stopped
    And no session turn or proof process outlives the cancel deadline

  @phase2 @ops @concurrency

scenarios.description: The heartbeat, the wall clock and the stale cadence run independently
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV5 The heartbeat, the wall clock and the stale cadence run independently
    Given a live run whose stale check is held on the checkout lock
    When the clock advances by 5 seconds
    Then the status file is touched once with a newer heartbeat
    And a touch that fails is logged and records no fact
    And the run wall clock records run.ended in state failed when it expires

  @phase2 @negative

scenarios.description: Three worker failures in a row fail the unit with a harness error
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV6 Three worker failures in a row fail the unit with a harness error
    Given a task supervisor whose worker fails
    When the worker fails three times in a row
    Then the supervisor records task.failed with a reason that starts "harness error:"
    And a scenario batch whose worker fails three times records its scenario fact the same way

  @phase2 @integrity @concurrency

scenarios.description: Facts enter only through the Recorder, in one order
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV7 Facts enter only through the Recorder, in one order
    Given two supervisors that record facts at the same moment
    When the Recorder stores and folds them
    Then the store order equals the fold order and the recorded times never decrease
    And a record after the run is done stores nothing
    And an interrupted record leaves either the whole fact or nothing

  @phase2 @permissions

scenarios.description: One run is live in a directory at a time (owner ruling 3)
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV8 One run is live in a directory at a time (owner ruling 3)
    Given a live run of the release-notes spec in a directory
    When /task runs for a valid spec in the same directory
    Then it starts nothing and answers one line that names the live run's spec and path
    And a claim whose background job does not start is released, so the next /task is not busy

  @phase2 @audit

scenarios.description: Supervisors record only facts the progress alphabet allows
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV9 Supervisors record only facts the progress alphabet allows
    Given each unit kind in each state
    When its supervisor records a fact
    Then the fact is in the progress alphabet for that state, or is a stall, a nudge, a run start, a resume, a spec check, a run-level stop or a stale obligation

  @phase2 @negative

scenarios.description: A stalled builder stream is cancelled and prompted again in the same attempt
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV10 A stalled builder stream is cancelled and prompted again in the same attempt
    Given a building task whose model stream goes quiet with no tool running
    When the stream idle time passes
    Then the turn is cancelled and task.stalled is recorded
    And the builder is prompted again with the continue message in the same attempt
    And no nudge and no attempt is spent

  @phase2 @negative

scenarios.description: A spend cap stops the task for a human before any nudge
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV11 A spend cap stops the task for a human before any nudge
    Given a building task
    When a retry status or the turn's error names the spend cap
    Then task.needs_human is recorded with a reason that starts "spend cap:"
    And no nudge is recorded

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: An idle builder is nudged twice, then the proof decides
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV12 An idle builder is nudged twice, then the proof decides
    Given a building task whose turn ends idle without task_ready
    When the turn ends idle a first and a second time
    Then task.nudged is recorded with nudge 1, then with nudge 2
    And after the last nudge the proof runs on the builder's head, or the task records "the builder ended without task_ready"

  @phase2 @permissions

scenarios.description: Harness tool calls reach the supervisor that owns the session
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV13 Harness tool calls reach the supervisor that owns the session
    Given a builder session claimed by its task supervisor
    When the builder calls task_ready, the verifier calls verdict, or the builder repeats a call past the limit
    Then the owner receives the event and records its fact when the turn ends
    And a session that no supervisor owns records nothing and the tool says so
    And every claim of a run is removed when the run ends

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: The session watch and the hooks hold no state of their own
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV14 The session watch and the hooks hold no state of their own
    Given the session watch and hook modules after phase 2
    When they are inspected
    Then they hold no Ref, no MutableHashMap and no polled loop
    And stall, idle and the spend cap are delayed transitions and guards of the task supervisor

  @phase2 @core

scenarios.description: The status file is a projection of the machine snapshot
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV15 The status file is a projection of the machine snapshot
    Given the observed facts folded through the release-notes machine
    When the status is projected
    Then each task, obligation and scenario carries its state, its tags, its blocked cause, its start and end times and, for a task, its spans
    And the run carries its title, spec id, path, start and end times, and each scenario carries its loader title with no leading id
    And the projection derives no state of its own and never emits phase or dependency tags
    And the old run-state and waitingOn derivations from the plan no longer exist
    And an obligation, which never blocks, carries no blocked cause

  @phase2 @integrity

scenarios.description: The status writer writes every committed step and stops at the end
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV16 The status writer writes every committed step and stops at the end
    Given a live run
    When facts are recorded and the heartbeat touches the file
    Then the file is written once for each committed macrostep, the final one included
    And each write stamps the heartbeat time
    And a touch rewrites the last consumed snapshot and never an older one
    And nothing writes the file after the done snapshot

  @phase2 @compat

scenarios.description: The TUI decodes the status file that the harness writes
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV17 The TUI decodes the status file that the harness writes
    Given the shared status fixture written by the harness projection with a fixed clock
    When the TUI decodes the fixture and a status file from before the change
    Then both decode
    And the fixture equals the projection of the observed facts byte for byte

  @phase2 @audit @critical

scenarios.description: The state audit fails on state held outside xstate
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: SV18 The state audit fails on state held outside xstate
    Given a source tree with one planted Ref, MutableHashMap, SynchronizedRef, FiberMap, setInterval, polled loop, module-level mutable let or list of lifecycle states
    When the audit runs
    Then it fails and names the file and the identifier
    And in the task-ui it also fails on a planted Effect.sleep or Schedule

    Given a full-screen design at 120 by 24 cells with 13 scenarios and 5 stopped tasks
    When the user presses pagedown and clicks a STOPPED line
    Then the region keeps at least 8 rows, the Peek activity lines shrink first, and every entry is reachable by scroll
    And the click selects the first task of the line
    And under 149 cells the Board's right pane sits below the board

  @phase4 @negative

scenarios.description: A summary that cannot be written does not hold the run open
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: UI23 A summary that cannot be written does not hold the run open
    Given a run whose root session was deleted before the run ends
    When the run machine reaches a final state
    Then the failed say is logged
    And the run supervisor reaches closed, the job ends and the directory lease is released
    And the next /task in the directory is not busy

  @phase4 @core

scenarios.description: The directory is free once the run machine is final, even while the summary waits
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: UI24 The directory is free once the run machine is final, even while the summary waits
    Given a root session whose turn waits on a permission prompt
    When the run actor reaches done
    Then the lease is released after the writer writes the done snapshot and before the summary
    And the next /task in the directory is not busy
    And the summary is written once, when the root turn ends, or its failure is logged when the root session goes away

  @phase4 @compat

scenarios.description: A status file from before the change is drawn with a defined fallback
scenarios.gherkin:
Scenario: UI25 A status file from before the change is drawn with a defined fallback
    Given a status file with no tags, no title and no heartbeat, as the old harness or the phase-1 code wrote it
    When each design renders it
    Then the view is still, and every design shows the muted line "status from an older harness — type /task to refresh"
    And the tasks show their glyph and state label from the display table, with no Board column, count or STOPPED group derived from them
